evidence.fact: Forestry advisory tools that combine remote sensing with AI already exist. Södra and Terra Labs' AI planner builds forest management plans, and Finnish chatbot-style advisors combine forest data, costs and legal requirements into recommendations. These tools speed up advisory work but are not meant to replace foresters.
In Alabama, anyone who gives forest management recommendations for hire on land they do not own must be registered with the state Board of Registration for Foresters.
California's Board of Forestry says that offering forestry recommendations on forested land without a Registered Professional Forester's expertise and stamp violates the Professional Foresters Law.

Jail management systems already automate parts of the release check. Tyler's DeKalb deployment halved release processing time and removed duplicate warrant data entry, and other systems recheck charges and warrants (NCIC) at release. Because warrant databases are split across agencies, a human still has to cross-check.
Deschutes County jail policy names the shift supervisor as the final safeguard in the release process. The supervisor must sign the Release Authorization Form before an inmate is released.
In Bexar County, two supervisors must approve each release, and staff who authorize a wrongful release can be disciplined. Legal accountability therefore stays with human supervisors.
The main salon platforms (Fresha, Boulevard, Vagaro, Mindbody) can keep a client's card on file and take deposits automatically. That lets software settle a bill without anyone at the counter.
Boulevard offers a self-checkout kiosk and an AI receptionist. Third-party AI receptionists connect to Vagaro's API to find clients, book appointments and take deposits.

The vendor sources say AI tools handle booking and deposits, but they don't confirm fully automatic checkout after a visit. Taking cash, making change and helping clients with tap or chip payments at the till still need a person there.

Shelf-scanning robots such as Simbe's Tally and Walmart's scanners find out-of-stock items, wrong prices and label problems on shelves. They give information to store associates, but people still do the physical cleaning and organizing. These are robots, which the reference AI agent does not have.
In 2026, agentic AI in retail is used for customer support, pricing and clienteling. It is described as a tool that helps associates, not as something that sells on the sales floor.
Walmart says its in-store inventory robots check shelves but will not replace store workers. The physical shelf work and selling face to face still need people.

Salesforce made its Agentforce Commerce Shopper Agent generally available in mid-2026 (June 24 or July 6; the sources give different dates). The agent answers consumer product questions, helps them find products and handles checkout on the retailer's own storefront.

The agents connect directly to inventory, order and customer data, so they can explain products and deal with service questions without passing the customer to a person. Commentators warn that answers drawn from the product catalogue can still be wrong, and no independent accuracy data was found.

Salesforce says AI influenced 20% of global online sales ($262B) during the 2025 holiday season. These are vendor figures. In physical stores, showing how a product works and building trust face to face still needs a person on the floor.

Industry commentary from 2026 says agentic AI can take a learning objective to a finished course: it analyzes source material, structures the content, builds personalized learning paths, role-plays and rubrics, and loads the course into an LMS. This evidence is mostly vendor or industry commentary, not independent outcome studies.

Courses on AI-powered instructional design for L&D professionals stress that human expertise is still essential for learning strategy and quality. These are marketing listings, not evidence of outcomes.

Canada's Job Bank lists Manager, Training and Development as not regulated. US career guides describe certification such as ATD or ISPI as voluntary, so no licence is generally required. A few roles, such as security training, have employer-specific credential requirements.

Coats Digital released GSD RealMotion in August 2026. It is an AI tool that turns shop-floor video into method studies and is designed to work alongside its existing GSDCost system. The vendor (not independent testing) says it cuts a 45-minute manual timing exercise to about 15 minutes. So AI speeds up key steps, but someone still has to film on the floor and check the results.

A proposed framework for AI-assisted MODAPTS calls for checking AI-generated standards against stopwatch or video time studies, with manual recoding when they differ by more than ±5%. That means a human still has to validate the work before standards are used.

In the US, industrial engineers usually don't need a PE license because many states have an industrial exemption. A license is generally needed only for stamping designs. So in most cases, no law or license requires a human to sign off on internal labor standards or cost systems.

Existing AI tools such as aiScout (ai.io), Hudl, Sportlogiq and Wyscout already analyze athlete video, score drills and generate performance data and scouting reports. This covers the record-review and much of the skill-assessment work.

A 2024 study of English academy scouts found no significant difference between ratings made in person and from video. However, scouts still considered in-person viewing more accurate, and it carries real time and travel costs.

Scouts still value live viewing for intangibles (work ethic, leadership, body language, off-ball behaviour) and use in-person events and tryouts. Evaluating physical fitness on site requires being there. No search result showed a licensing rule requiring a human scout.
